title: Representation tensor and finite scalar comparisons of a normalized fibre equivalence
statement: With finite correspondence data d of [def-pod-galois-correspondence-data-e4], suppose its action agrees on section germs with evaluation on the finite locally constant underlying sheaf and its constant coefficient module is the trivial representation. Every braided monoidal structure on the lisse R-module category whose inclusion into the actual sheaf tensor category is braided makes its representation functor braided, for finite commutative R. For all finite ring maps R → S, suppose actual sheafified balanced scalar-extension functors B and natural underlying-sheaf comparisons α are supplied. Suppose also that scalar extension commutes with the unlifted geometric module stalk, by a natural isomorphism sending a tensor germ(s) to the germ of the sheafified a tensor s. Suppose also natural composite comparisons c are supplied and satisfy the section identity sending b tensor (a tensor s) to b g(a) tensor s. There are natural representation comparisons β with the representation composite identity in galoisFiniteScalarExtension for these same c. The monoidal structure of the sheaf subcategory itself is a hypothesis here, not part of this obligation.

proof.text: Transport the canonical tensor-stalk isomorphism through d.τ. Naturality of the evaluation automorphisms on the bilinear sheaf map gives equivariance on pure tensors, with the diagonal action. Pure tensors generate; the source tensor-stalk coherence proves associativity, symmetry and unit compatibility. Use the assumed unit identification to obtain the braided representation functor.

Use the supplied scalar-extension functors B and their underlying-sheaf comparisons. The supplied unlifted scalar stalk comparison and its germ formula make it equivariant by naturality on each set map s ↦ a tensor s. Transport it through d.τ to obtain β. The supplied composite comparison c has the normalized section formula hc. Its stalk comparison therefore agrees on pure tensors with the source scalar associator, and the source stalk-composition theorem proves the representation composite identity for this same c.
